theater: 克里特島北部與西部海岸

battle.name: 庫倫事件
battle.theater: 克里特島北部與西部海岸
battle.brief: 公元前六三〇年代，薩伊特王朝埃及為報復斯巴達的羞辱，遣雅典人福爾米翁率艦隊遠征克里特島，暗助島上殘存的伊提奧克里特人。海戰埃及與克里特方得手，斯巴達戰艦登陸後仍以重裝步兵方陣逆轉，末了得埃伊達援軍之助，克里特殘部覆滅。卡面的埃及長矛為早王朝青銅形制，本役現場已改用鐵刃長矛。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場衝突是薩伊特王朝埃及與斯巴達為爭奪克里特島而在公元前七世紀末爆發的一場戰爭，希腊史料通常稱之為克里特之役。埃及一方由尼羅河三角洲的薩伊特王權直接統轄，國王派遣一支以三列槳船為主體的皇家艦隊，艦上除埃及水手外，還有大批卡里亞人與愛奧尼亞人雇傭兵，以及為數不多的腓尼基與希臘船員；指揮系統由法老直屬的將領與一名雅典提督福爾米翁組成，海軍是這次遠征的主體，陸軍只留少量步兵與弓手在克里特東岸支援。克里特島的一方是所謂「真正的克里特人」，即多利安人征服島嶼之後仍留居西部山區的舊居民後裔，他們人數有限，以弓、投槍與戰斧作戰，沒有希臘式重裝步兵的裝備與陣形。斯巴達一方則以公民戰士組成的重裝步兵為核心，配以伯羅奔尼撒同盟諸城邦提供的戰艦，企圖把這批島民納入斯巴達的勢力範圍。最後加入戰局的埃伊達是斯巴達的海上盟友，以數十艘三列槳船趕到，與斯巴達殘餘艦隊合流，在最後一場陸戰中扭轉局勢。這是一場典型的、以海軍投射為主的遠征式衝突，雙方的實力差距主要體現在艦隊規模與航海經驗上。
countriesEn: This clash was a war fought in the closing years of the seventh century BC between the Saite dynasty of Egypt and Sparta, each of them contesting control of the island of Crete; the Greek sources usually call it the Cretan campaign. On the Egyptian side the command lay directly with the Saite kingship of the Nile delta: the king sent out a royal fleet built around triremes, manned not only by Egyptian sailors but by large numbers of Carian and Ionian mercenaries together with a few Phoenician and Greek hands; the chain of command ran from the king through his own commanders to an Athenian admiral, Phormion. For this expedition the navy was the main instrument, while only a small body of infantry and archers was kept on the east coast of Crete to support it. The Cretan side were the so-called Eteocretans, the descendants of the island's older inhabitants who remained in the western mountains after the Dorians had taken Crete; their numbers were small, they fought with bows, javelins and battle-axes, and they possessed neither the equipment nor the formation of Greek hoplites. The Spartan side was built on citizen heavy infantry, with the warships contributed by the other cities of the Peloponnesian league, and aimed to draw the islanders into Sparta's sphere of influence. Aegina, Sparta's maritime ally, entered the war at the end with several tens of triremes, joined the remnant of the Spartan fleet, and reversed the situation in the final land battle. In short, this was a typical expedition fought by sea power projected overseas, and the imbalance between the sides lay mainly in the size of the fleets and in seamanship.
people: 最關鍵的人物是日後登基為法老的阿摩西斯。希羅多德在《歷史》第一卷第六十六節講述他的來歷：他的父親原是低賤的腹語者，他本人則以模仿他人的口音與舉止取悅王室，成為王室中的一名近侍；後來他掌握了在法老面前的分量，被派去執行一件帶有羞辱性質的差事——斯巴達國王本以為他斃死的是一名冒犯國王的樂師，正要重賞，卻查出那其實是王后的私生兒，勃然大怒之下下令鞭打，他便逃回埃及。斯巴達人派船到埃及要求引渡，埃及方面把他交出來，斯巴達人又當眾鞭打了他一頓；從此他記恨斯巴達，策劃了這場以克里特為戰場的遠征。法老本人是薩伊特王朝的君主，現存材料對是普薩姆提克一世還是其子尼科二世仍有分歧，編年多把此役繫於前六三〇年代。艦隊統帥是雅典人福爾米翁，他是這場戰役中唯一留下姓名的指揮官；同名者在前四七九年米卡列之戰中亦曾率雅典艦隊作戰，學界多認為是兩人。斯巴達的統帥沒有留下姓名，只知是斯巴達海軍的統率者；克里特殘軍與埃伊達援軍的首領同樣無名。記錄這場戰爭的是五世紀的希臘史家希羅多德，距事實約兩百年，他所憑據的多是口耳相傳的說法，數字與人名都須打折看。
peopleEn: The decisive figure is Ahmasis, later to become pharaoh. In Histories I.66 Herodotus tells of his origins: his father was a humble ventriloquist, and he himself rose by imitating the voices and manners of others, becoming a favourite at court; he then acquired enough standing in front of the king to be given a commission that carried an insult with it — the Spartan king believed he had killed a flute-player who had offended the king and meant to reward him, only to discover that the man was the queen's illegitimate son, and in his rage ordered him to be whipped, whereupon he fled to Egypt. The Spartans sent a ship to Egypt to demand his surrender; the Egyptians handed him over, and the Spartans whipped him publicly in turn. From that day he held the Spartans in bitter memory, and this expedition to Crete was his way of striking back. The king himself was the ruler of the Saite dynasty; the surviving material disagrees over whether this was Psammetichus I or his son Necho II, and the chronographers usually place the campaign in the 630s BC. The commander of the fleet was Phormion of Athens, the only commander of this war whose name survives. A man of the same name commanded the Athenian fleet at Mycale in 479 BC, and most scholars treat them as two different people. The Spartan commander left no name behind, only the fact that he was the ruler of the Spartan navy; the leaders of the Cretan remnants and of the Aeginetan reinforcement are likewise nameless. The war is recorded by the fifth-century Greek historian Herodotus, writing roughly two centuries after the events, and his account rests largely on oral tradition, so both his numbers and his names have to be taken with a discount.
kits: 卡面這支「埃及長矛」是早王朝時代的形制：寬大的銅質矛頭以榫眼或綁紮方式固定在木杆上，用途偏向守城與近身格鬥。本役距其定型已逾三千年，薩伊特王朝的長矛已是另一副樣貌：矛頭改用鐵或精煉銅，形制更細長挺直，杆身加長，握持位置與配重都為面對方陣密集推進而調整，與卡面那支寬刃短裝的守城長矛只餘同源之別。埃及步兵的編制可由希羅多德第二卷第一六八節得知：每個連隊四百四十一人，其中長矛手二百、弓箭手二百、輕盾兵四十一，另有每年從各地挑選、以鑲金盾牌與青銅盔武裝的法老近衛。埃及的護具與弓弩也自成體系：盾牌取尼羅河鱷魚皮製成、鑲嵌金屬飾件，弓身短而硬，射程雖近但射速極快。斯巴達與埃伊達的戰士則是典型希臘重裝步兵：青銅頭盔、胸前甲胄、大圓盾，列成密集方陣；其海軍以三列槳船為骨幹，甲板上編入重裝步兵，遠射武器則是投槍與弓。克里特一方沒有金屬甲胄式的防護，靠弓、投槍與克里特式雙刃斧作戰，並善用島上的峽灣與山徑。除此之外，這場戰爭沒有攻城器械與重型運輸工具的記載，埃及遠征的主要非人力裝備是船隻本身，以及由尼羅河運河與沿岸港口組成的補給線。
kitsEn: The spear on the card is an early dynastic form: a broad copper or bronze head fixed to a wooden shaft by tang or binding, intended for defence of walls and for close fighting. This campaign came more than three millennia after that form was fixed, and the spears of the Saite dynasty looked quite different: the heads were made of iron or refined copper, the profile was longer and straighter, the shaft was lengthened, and the point of balance and the grip were readjusted for the shock of massed formations advancing on them. The card's wide-bladed, short-mounted spear for wall defence is therefore related to the weapon of this war only in its ancestry. The organisation of Egyptian infantry can be read from Herodotus II.168: each company numbered 441 men, made up of 200 spearmen, 200 archers and 41 peltasts, alongside a body of royal guards selected each year from across the country and armed with metal-shod shields and bronze helmets. Egyptian armour and archery formed a system of their own: shields were made from Nile crocodile hide and fitted with metal ornaments, and the bows were short and hard, sacrificing range for a very high rate of shot. The Spartan and Aeginetan troops were in the classic Greek heavy-infantry mode — bronze helmet, cuirass, large round shield, ranked in a dense phalanx; their navies were built on triremes with heavy infantry crowded on the decks, and their missile weapons were javelins and bows. The Cretans had no metal body armour to speak of, relying on bows, javelins and the double-bladed axe that is a Cretan emblem, and they knew how to use the island's ravines and mountain paths. Beyond this, the war leaves no record of siege engines or heavy transport; the Egyptians' chief non-manpower assets were the ships themselves and the supply line formed by the Nile canals and the coastal ports.
tactics: 海戰是這場戰爭的第一階段，也是埃及遠征方最能發揮優勢的環節。埃及艦隊自尼羅河三角洲出航，沿非洲北岸與克里特之間的航線北上，選擇島嶼東岸的開闊海面展開；其基本戰法是避免與希臘式三列槳船正面纏鬥，改以弓弩與投石在遠距離傾瀉，削弱敵船的甲板人員，再以數量優勢分割、包抄殘餘敵船。克里特方以岸上弓兵配合，海上多靠漁船與小型舟艇接應，使斯巴達人無法痛快登岸。斯巴達在海戰失利後並未撤走，而是收攏殘存船艦，選擇克里特西岸一段適合重裝步兵展開的地形登陸，企圖以方陣正面突破在山區活動的島民；這一轉折把一場海戰變成了陸戰，也讓斯巴達的兵種優勢重新生效。最後的關鍵步驟是求援：斯巴達立刻派快船渡海前往埃伊達，說明當時的消息傳遞仍完全依靠單列快船，數百里航程往往要數日乃至數週；埃伊達援軍抵達後，斯巴達得以把艦隊與登陸部隊重新捏合，聯手完成對島民的殲滅性攻擊。就補給而言，埃及遠征跨越約五百公里的地中海航程，糧食與飲水全靠船隊自運，士兵在甲板上下起居，效率低而消耗大，一旦戰局膠著，遠征方最先感到的便是糧秣與傷患累積的壓力。
tacticsEn: The sea battle was the first phase of the war and the phase in which the Egyptian expedition could best play to its strength. The fleet left the Nile delta, sailed north along the route between the African coast and Crete, and deployed in the open water off the island's east coast. Its basic method was to avoid a straight engagement with Greek triremes and instead pour arrows and stones into the enemy at long range, thinning the crews on their decks, and then to use its numerical superiority to split up and encircle the surviving enemy ships. The Cretans supported from the shore with archers, and at sea they relied on fishing craft and small boats to harass the Spartans and prevent them from landing undisturbed. After the naval defeat Sparta did not withdraw but gathered the surviving ships, chose a stretch of the west coast where heavy infantry could deploy, and landed in order to break the islanders in the open with the phalanx; that turn turned a naval war into a land battle and let the Spartan advantage in arms reassert itself. The decisive last step was the appeal for help: Sparta at once sent fast ships across the sea to Aegina, which shows that news still travelled entirely on single-oared fast vessels, and that a few hundred kilometres of sea usually cost days or weeks. Once the Aeginetan reinforcement arrived, Sparta could weld its fleet and its landed troops back together and complete the decisive stroke against the islanders. On the logistics side, the Egyptian expedition covered roughly five hundred kilometres of open sea, with food and water carried entirely in the ships, the soldiers living on the decks, an arrangement that was inefficient and costly; once the fighting stalled, it was the grain and the accumulating sick and wounded that the expeditionary force felt first.
data: 可核對的數字並不多，以下幾項有較明確的來源。第一，埃及步兵的連隊編制為四百四十一人，含長矛手二百、弓箭手二百、輕盾兵四十一，此為希羅多德第二卷第一六八節所記的薩伊特王朝軍制。第二，埃伊達派出的援軍，通行解作三十艘三列槳船；也有學者解作更小的數目，爭議主要在抄本異文。第三，埃及艦隊的總數在希臘、埃及兩系記載中互有出入，一般落在二百至三百艘之間，人數以萬計，狄奧多羅斯一系給出較具體的說法；希羅多德則以語氣強調埃及艦隊遠勝於斯巴達，具體數目不載。第四，地理距離方面，由尼羅河三角洲的港口到克里特島北部約五百公里，雅典到克里特島北岸約五百公里，埃伊達到克里特島約二百五十至三百公里，這幾個數字說明求援與補給都不是當天可以往返的事。第五，年代方面，多數編年把此役繫於公元前六三一年，部分學者放寬到前六三三年至前六三〇年之間。就戰役本身而言，現存記載顯示海戰、登陸陸戰、求援、援軍抵達與最後決戰都集中在同一個戰役年度之內完成。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few, and the following are the ones with a reasonably clear basis. First, the Egyptian company was 441 strong, with 200 spearmen, 200 archers and 41 peltasts, which is Herodotus' account of the Saite military system in II.168. Second, the Aeginetan reinforcement is conventionally read as thirty triremes, though some scholars interpret the figure as smaller; the dispute turns on variant readings of the manuscripts. Third, the total size of the Egyptian fleet differs between the Greek and Egyptian lines of evidence, generally falling between two and three hundred ships with a force in the tens of thousands; Diodorus gives the more specific figure, while Herodotus simply stresses how far the Egyptian fleet outnumbered the Spartan one and records no number at all. Fourth, as to distances, the run from the ports of the Nile delta to northern Crete is about five hundred kilometres, from Athens to the north coast of Crete about five hundred, and from Aegina to Crete about two hundred and fifty to three hundred; these figures show that neither an appeal for help nor a resupply was a same-day errand. Fifth, as to date, most chronologies put the campaign in 631 BC, while some scholars widen it to somewhere between 633 and 630 BC. As for the campaign itself, the surviving record shows that the sea battle, the landing, the appeal, the arrival of the reinforcement and the final decision all took place within a single campaigning year.
cause: 打起來有兩層原因，遠因與近因交疊。遠因在克里特島本身：多利安人入主島嶼之後，舊有的居民被逐步排擠到西部山區，殘餘者就是希臘人所稱的「真正的克里特人」。前七世紀末，斯巴達的勢力向克里特推進，雙方為島上的土地、牧場與港口控制權對峙不斷，這場戰爭正是這條擴張線上的正面碰撞。近因則在埃及：薩伊特王朝雖在亞述壓力下節節退卻，仍握有尼羅河三角洲的財富與一支規模可觀的僱傭兵軍隊，於是把克里特當成削弱斯巴達、又不必直接冒犯斯巴達本土的試驗場；阿摩西斯受辱之後需要一個反擊的機會，而克里特正好提供了一個可用的戰場。背後還有地中海航運的經濟算計：控制克里特海峽，就等於卡住愛琴海與腓尼基、埃及之間的東地中海航線；那條航線正是薩伊特王朝最重要的外貿通道。再加上克里特在傳統上產弓、產弓匠與產兵，海上遠征需要大量希臘與卡里亞雇傭兵，而雅典的水手恰好是最被信任的海上雇傭力量之一——福爾米翁的指揮權正是這樣交到雅典人手上。
causeEn: There were two layers of cause, a distant one and an immediate one overlapping. The distant cause lay on Crete itself: after the Dorians had taken the island, the older inhabitants were gradually pushed back into the western mountains, and the survivors of that population are what the Greeks called the true Cretans. In the closing years of the seventh century BC Sparta's influence pushed forward into Crete, and the two sides collided openly over land, pasture and harbours — this war is that collision on the line of expansion. The immediate cause lay in Egypt: although the Saite dynasty was being worn down by Assyrian pressure, it still held the wealth of the Nile delta and a sizeable force of mercenaries, and it therefore took Crete as a testing ground on which to weaken Sparta without striking at the Spartan homeland itself; and after his humiliation Ahmasis needed a chance to hit back, which Crete happened to provide. Behind this lay the economic arithmetic of Mediterranean shipping: control of the Cretan straits meant a stranglehold on the east Mediterranean sea lane between the Aegean and Phoenicia and Egypt, and that lane was the Saite dynasty's most important trade route. There was also the old reputation of Crete for bows, bow-makers and soldiers, so a distant expedition needed large numbers of Greek and Carian mercenaries, and Athenian sailors were among the most trusted hirelings at sea — which is precisely how the command passed to an Athenian.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接後果，是克里特島落入斯巴達一系的手中，島上殘餘的舊居民退往山區或被編入斯巴達的盟邦體系；其後一百年裡，島上出現克諾索斯、戈爾提納、利托斯等由多利安人建立的城邦，克里特也隨之進入伯羅奔尼撒同盟的版圖，島上的希臘化進程與主陸關係從此密不可分。第二個後果在埃伊達：這座島城因聲稱自己獨力完成了最後的勝利而名聲大振，開始以「希臘第二強邦」自居，此後與雅典在海路上的競爭、以及它在薩摩斯島的殖民地問題，都成為希波戰爭爆發前夜希臘世界的一枚不安的棋子。第三個後果在埃及：這次遠征展現了薩伊特王朝海上力量的頂點，也暴露了它對希臘雇傭兵的高度依賴；不久之後尼科二世揮師敘利亞，最終在迦基米什被巴比倫王尼布甲尼撒二世擊敗，薩伊特王朝的霸權就此收束，克里特之役因而被視為埃及帝國在擴張與收縮之間的一個轉折點。阿摩西斯本人後來把大量土地賜給埃伊達人，作為他們「出戰有功」的回報，這份人情也牽動了後來雅典與埃伊達之間的糾葛。
impactEn: The immediate consequence was that Crete fell to the Spartan side, with the surviving islanders driven back into the mountains or absorbed into Sparta's league system; over the following century the island produced Dorian-founded poleis such as Knossos, Gortyn and Lyttos, and Crete entered the Peloponnesian league, its Hellenisation henceforth inseparable from that of the mainland. The second consequence fell on Aegina: the island city grew famous by claiming that it had won the final victory unaided, began to style itself the second power of Greece, and its later rivalry with Athens at sea, together with its colony on Samos, became one of the uneasy pieces on the Greek board on the eve of the Persian Wars. The third consequence fell on Egypt: this expedition showed the summit of the Saite naval power and exposed how completely the dynasty leaned on Greek mercenaries; not long afterwards Necho II marched into Syria and was beaten at Carchemish by Nebuchadnezzar II, and the Saite hegemony closed up, so the Cretan enterprise is usually read as a turning point between Egyptian expansion and contraction. Ahmasis himself later granted land to the Aeginetans as a reward for their service in the war, and that debt was to have a say in the later quarrels between Athens and Aegina.
result: 戰局是三段式的：第一段海戰，埃及艦隊在克里特島外海擊敗斯巴達分艦隊，克里特方得以維持抵抗，這是埃及遠征方唯一確定的勝利；第二段登陸，斯巴達收拾殘船登陸，以重裝步兵的方陣在克里特島西部擊潰伊提奧克里特人的隊伍，把島上的抵抗壓回山區；第三段援軍，斯巴達急赴埃伊達求援，得到數十艘船的援軍，聯軍再戰，克里特殘軍遭到決定性的失敗，倖存者退入山區或流散。整體而言，埃及用一次大規模海軍遠征換來了一場海上的勝利，卻沒有換來克里特島的歸屬，也沒有真正削弱斯巴達；反倒是援軍埃伊達收穫了全部的戰功名聲。對斯巴達而言，這是一場代價不菲卻最終成功的遠征，島嶼納入其勢力範圍，通往克里特海峽的航路被徹底清障。對薩伊特王朝的埃及而言，此役證明其海上遠征的組織與補給能力，也同時暴露了王朝的隱患：真正能打的希臘人不是埃及人自己，而是受雇於法老的雅典人與卡里亞人；一旦王朝的財政或王朝繼承出現裂縫，這支「借來的軍隊」就會成為內部最不穩定的因素。
resultEn: The course of the war ran in three stages. In the first, the sea battle, the Egyptian fleet beat the Spartan squadron off Crete and the Cretan side was able to keep the resistance alive — the one victory the expeditionary side can be certain of. In the second, the landing, Sparta collected what was left of its fleet, put ashore, and broke the Eteocretans in western Crete with the phalanx of heavy infantry, driving the resistance back into the mountains. In the third, the reinforcement, Sparta hurried to Aegina for help, obtained several tens of ships, and fought again; the Cretan remnants suffered a decisive defeat and the survivors fled into the hills or scattered. On balance, Egypt had traded a large naval expedition for a victory at sea, and got neither the island nor any real weakening of Sparta; instead the relieving Aegina walked away with all the credit for the victory. For Sparta this was a costly but ultimately successful expedition: the island was brought into its sphere and the sea lane through the Cretan straits was cleared of all opposition. For Saite Egypt the campaign proved the organisation and the supply capacity of its long-range naval warfare, and at the same time exposed the dynasty's weakness — the men who actually fought were not Egyptians but Athenians and Carians in Egyptian pay, and the moment the dynasty's finances or its succession cracked, that borrowed army would become the most unstable element inside the state.
